summary: Instagram is carrying the channel: most Hindi videos get 1,200-1,400 views there, while YouTube Shorts mostly get under 60 views. The best videos use a surprising 'it doesn't see/hear/think the way you expect' hook about a robot, clap switch or sensor, and they lead in likes and saves. Questions about everyday places (lift, mall door, tap, street light) and generic 'how does X work' titles get far fewer views, and the one English video got no Instagram reach.
winningPattern: Hindi videos on hands-on maker subjects (robots, clap switch, PIR/IR/heat sensors, mic) with a myth-busting hook that says the device lacks a human ability ('doesn't see', 'has no brain', 'only hears noise'). Short titles, one emoji, #shorts, posted on Instagram first. Titles that start from the surprising statement outperform 'How does X know...?' questions about everyday public gadgets. YouTube performs best on the same robot/clap/PIR topics, so those themes work on both platforms.
doMore: Open with a bold negative claim: 'X can't see/hear/think, yet...'
Make follow-ups to the winners: clap switch, gyro robot, line follower, PIR sensor, mic
Pick Arduino and robot-building subjects that makers can copy or try
Post to Instagram first, then YouTube, and track them separately
Add a save-worthy ending, like a part name or wiring tip, since saves and shares signal quality
stopDoing: Generic 'Kaise Kaam Karta Hai?' question titles on everyday public gadgets (lift, mall door, taps, smoke alarms)
Publishing near-duplicate topics in the same week (three smoke/tap/IR videos split the audience)
English narration until you test it with a proper Instagram version
